title: Videonystagmography (VNG)
what: The doctor records your eye movements with special goggles that have cameras. Your eyes show how the balance organ in your inner ear works.
why: For dizziness, unsteady walking, ringing in the ears, or after a head injury, to find the cause.
duration: usually 30 to 60 minutes; the report is often ready the same day
tell_doctor: What medicines you take, especially for dizziness, sedatives, and sleeping pills
If your neck or back hurts. Some head turns can be replaced
If you have eye problems or see poorly without glasses
If you have a hole in your eardrum or recent ear surgery

prepare.title: Medicines
prepare.text: Some medicines interfere with the test. Do not stop them on your own. Tell your doctor. They will decide what can be skipped and for how many days.

prepare.title: Food and alcohol
prepare.text: No alcohol for 1 to 2 days before. You are usually asked not to eat a big meal for 2 to 3 hours before, because you may feel sick.

prepare.title: Face
prepare.text: Come without eye makeup. Mascara gets in the way of the camera.

prepare.title: Getting home
prepare.text: You may feel a little dizzy after the test. Better not to drive right away. Bring someone with you.

steps: You sit in a chair, and goggles with cameras are put on
First, you follow a dot on a screen with your eyes
Then your head and body positions are changed: lying down, on your side, with turns
Sometimes warm and cool air or water is put in each ear. This tests each ear separately
The doctor watches your eye movements on a monitor
feel: During some tests you feel dizzy and may feel sick. This is expected and passes quickly
Tell the doctor if you feel very unwell. They will take a break
after: Sit for 10 to 15 minutes until the dizziness passes
You can go on with your normal day
The report is often ready right away, sometimes in 1 to 2 days
red_flags: A severe headache, double vision, weakness in an arm or leg, or trouble speaking: call emergency services right away

faq.q: Why do I get dizzy during the test?
faq.a: Some tests cause brief dizziness on purpose. This shows the doctor how the balance organ responds.

faq.q: Can I take dizziness pills before the VNG?
faq.a: They can change the result. Tell your doctor in advance. They will decide if you need a break.

reminders.text: VNG tomorrow. No eye makeup, no big meal for 2 to 3 hours before, and bring someone with you.
